saas-integration-manager.useWhen: Admins review connected apps, see which syncs are failing and exactly what data each scope moves, then reconnect or change access through the provider.
saas-integration-manager.avoidWhen: You are building a public marketplace or storing credentials in the browser; this surface reviews and triggers authorisation, the provider and your server hold the tokens.
integration: Each integration lists `scopes` with access (read or write), objects, purpose and whether it is required; read lanes point into the workspace and write lanes point out.
`onAuthorize` receives { integrationId, mode, scopes }: open the provider's OAuth window and resolve once the token is stored (optionally with `expiresAt`), or reject with the provider's error.
Feed `history` with 24 hourly { ok, failed } buckets and `lastSyncAt`, and pass `now`, so the board reads true.
Monograms stand in for vendor marks; swap in licensed logos in your own build if you have them.

saas-notification-inbox.useWhen: People triage a stream of mentions, alerts, access requests and system notices and want to clear it from the keyboard: archive with undo, snooze to a time they can see, and read counts per source.
saas-notification-inbox.avoidWhen: You need a chat thread, a ticket queue with SLAs (use saas-support-triage), or a page that only lists recent changes without acting on them.
integration: Pass notifications as { id, source, title, context, actor?, body?, at, read?, snoozedUntil?, metric?, facts?, actionLabel? }; `source` is one of mention, alert, access, report, integration or billing, and decides the group and icon.

`onAction` receives read, unread, archive, unarchive, snooze (with an ISO `until`) and unsnooze. Reads and archives are optimistic and roll back with an alert if it rejects; a snooze waits for it, and a rejection keeps the dialog open with the chosen time.
Pass `now` as the current time and `timeZone` for the reader; snooze presets (later today, tomorrow, Monday, next week) and the scrubber’s nights are computed in that zone.

Keys: J/K or arrows move and read, E archives, S snoozes, U toggles read, Z undoes, Enter calls `onOpen`. They are ignored while typing. Duplicate ids and unreadable times are left out and named in an alert.

saas-report-scheduler.useWhen: People schedule a recurring email report: they choose sections, cadence, delivery time, time zone and recipients, and want to see the report and its next deliveries before saving.
saas-report-scheduler.avoidWhen: You need a one-off export or a notification preference matrix; actual delivery and daylight-saving handling must happen on your server.
integration: Describe each section with a `kind` and optional `preview` data so the page renders it; sections without previews draw as skeletons.
Pass `now` as the current time; upcoming deliveries are computed in the schedule's IANA time zone for display, and your scheduler stays the source of truth.
`onSave` and `onSendTest` receive the full schedule; reject either to keep the draft and show the failure.
Set `workspaceDomain` so recipients outside your organisation are flagged as external before a report leaves the building.

saas-saved-views.useWhen: People slice the same records table repeatedly and want named, shareable views whose filters, columns and sort apply live, with a clear diff before anything is saved.
saas-saved-views.avoidWhen: You need a free-form query language or nested boolean logic; this offers ready-made filters per column, combined with AND.
integration: Describe the table with `columns` (key, label, kind, required, score scale) and pass plain `rows`; the kind decides the cell, the sort and the filter wording.
`views` hold { filters, columns, sort, shared, owner }. Views owned by someone other than `currentUser` can only be saved as a copy.
`onSave` receives { mode: "update" | "create", view }; resolve with the stored view to adopt a server id, or reject to keep the unsaved changes on screen.
Pass `today` so `withinDays` filters and renewal countdowns are measured from the real date; mirror `onViewChange` into the URL if views should be linkable.

saas-support-triage.useWhen: A support team routes incoming tickets into priority queues with an owner, watching first-reply SLAs count down on every ticket as they go.
saas-support-triage.avoidWhen: You are building the reply composer or a customer-facing help centre; this surface routes and assigns but never messages the customer.
integration: Tickets without a `priority` wait in the inbox; ones with a priority start in their queue. Clocks run from each `receivedAt` against your `sla` minutes.
Pass `now` as the current time; the clocks then tick in real time and pause while the component is off screen or the tab is hidden.
`onTriage` receives { ticketId, priority, assigneeId }; reject it and the ticket returns to the inbox with the error shown. `onUndo` mirrors the toast's Undo.
Keys 1–4 route the open ticket and J/K move through the inbox, so agents can triage without the mouse.
Resolve onUndo to restore the prior queue or inbox. Reject to keep the route and expose a retry. Invalid ticket/message timestamps are flagged; timing stays unavailable for those records.

saas-usage-policy.useWhen: Admins set warning thresholds, hard limits and enforcement for metered resources and need to see when current or simulated usage would cross them this billing period.
saas-usage-policy.avoidWhen: You need a customer-facing price estimate or a plan comparison; metering and enforcement themselves must run on your server, not in this editor.
integration: Pass each meter's `daily` usage (one value per elapsed day) with its current `warnAt`, `limit`, `enforcement` and `notifyAdmins`.
Set `periodStart` and `periodDays` so crossing dates and the reset date read correctly; `growth` seeds the demand simulator.
`onSave` receives every meter's policy at once; reject to keep the draft and show the failure in the save bar.
Provide `consequences` per meter so each enforcement option explains exactly what happens to that resource.

saas-workspace-dashboard.useWhen: The home screen of a SaaS workspace: a few headline metrics compared with the previous period, a trend you can read day by day, plan usage against limits, the most used dashboards and what the team just did.
saas-workspace-dashboard.avoidWhen: You need an editable report builder, a single deep chart with many series (use chart-revenue-trend), or status monitoring with alerting.
integration: Each metric is { id, label, daily, rollup, format?, better? }: one value per day ending on `today`. 180 days of history gives every range a previous period to compare with; shorter history reads “No prior period” rather than inventing one.
`rollup` decides the KPI figure (sum for events, mean for people per day or durations, last for a running total) and `better: "down"` makes a falling figure read as good news.

The range can be controlled with `range` and `onRangeChange` or left to `defaultRange`. `plan.meters` turn amber at 75% and red at 90%; `onManagePlan` shows the footer link and `onOpenDashboard` makes table rows open.
Set `loading` while data is on its way: skeletons hold the layout and the count-up entrance plays once it lands.

scroll-background-wipe.useWhen: A two-scene moment where the change itself is the story, such as night to day or before and after, with figures that travel with the reveal.
scroll-background-wipe.avoidWhen: Content that must be read during the transition, or more than two states; use a chapter stack or a sticky feature list instead.
integration: Set both scenes with `opening`, `closing`, their notes and bodies. `readouts` takes up to three { label, from, to } figures; use `format: "clock"` for minutes after midnight and `scale: "log"` for quantities such as light.
`origin` places the start of the reveal and the sun; `accent` colours only the sun. Reduced motion, or copy too tall for the viewport, stacks both complete scenes in ordinary flow.

scroll-chapter-stack.useWhen: A case study or story told in three to six chapters, each with a photograph, a few figures and enough copy to read without scrolling inside it.
scroll-chapter-stack.avoidWhen: Reference content people scan and compare, or chapters longer than a screen; those flow as ordinary sections and the stacking adds nothing.
integration: Pass your chapters through `chapters`, each with a stable `id`, an `eyebrow` that doubles as its jump-button label, real `imageSrc` and meaningful `imageAlt`. `facts` prints up to four short figures.

Stacking only engages on fine pointers in containers at least 760px wide where every chapter fits the viewport; otherwise, and with reduced motion, chapters flow in normal order. Keep ancestors free of overflow clipping so sticky positioning works.

scroll-cinema-frame.useWhen: A film page or launch story where a single video deserves the whole viewport, introduced with its title and credits.
scroll-cinema-frame.avoidWhen: Background loops, autoplay or galleries of several videos; this frame always waits for the visitor to press play.
integration: Pass host-owned `videoSrc`, `posterSrc` and WebVTT `captionSrc`. Playback stays native, never autoplays and pauses when the section leaves the viewport or the tab is hidden; a failed source shows the poster with a notice.
Without a video the drawn poster still is shown with its `posterLabel`, and the title card returns as the frame opens. `credits` lists up to four { label, value } pairs.

scroll-expanding-mosaic.useWhen: Opening a visual mosaic into a larger product or editorial moment.
scroll-expanding-mosaic.avoidWhen: A dense interactive grid whose controls become hard to reach while scrolling.
integration: Supply your own records through `tiles`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.

scroll-horizontal-showcase.useWhen: A short horizontal product sequence driven by a readable vertical story.
scroll-horizontal-showcase.avoidWhen: A long catalogue or content that can only be reached with a precise scroll gesture.
integration: Supply your own records through `projects`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.

scroll-image-curtain.useWhen: Revealing paired visuals through a controlled scroll progression.
scroll-image-curtain.avoidWhen: A before-and-after claim without authentic paired assets and clear context.
integration: Use the documented props to replace sample copy and connect the component to its surrounding page. The usage example below imports the production export.

text-decode.useWhen: A short decorative text reveal in an introductory section.
text-decode.avoidWhen: Body text, instructions or text that must remain immediately readable.
integration: Use the documented props to replace sample copy and connect the component to its surrounding page. The usage example below imports the production export.

three-ascii-object.useWhen: A restrained generative object within a creative or developer brand page.
three-ascii-object.avoidWhen: Essential information available only through the 3D scene or ASCII rendering.
integration: Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

three-contour-terrain.useWhen: An atmospheric terrain visual behind a clear editorial message.
three-contour-terrain.avoidWhen: A geographic map or quantitative landscape without an actual data model.
integration: Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

three-globe-arcs.useWhen: Illustrating supplied routes or connections on a globe.
three-globe-arcs.avoidWhen: A geographic authority or fabricated coverage and routing claims.
integration: Supply your own records through `routes`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.
Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

three-holo-card.useWhen: A decorative material treatment for a supplied card or brand visual.
three-holo-card.avoidWhen: A real product represented by an unrelated synthetic 3D object.
integration: Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

three-keycaps.useWhen: Explaining a small set of keyboard shortcuts with tactile key visuals.
three-keycaps.avoidWhen: The only accessible shortcut reference or shortcuts your product does not implement.
integration: Supply your own records through `rows`, `chords`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.
Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

three-particle-sphere.useWhen: A restrained generative scene in a landing-page introduction.
three-particle-sphere.avoidWhen: An essential data visualisation or an effect competing with reading and interaction.
integration: Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

three-voice-orb.useWhen: A decorative visual accompanying clearly labelled voice states.
three-voice-orb.avoidWhen: A microphone permission mechanism or voice state inferred solely from animation.
integration: Supply your own records through `speakingLines`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.
Keep this scene in a bounded visual region and retain ordinary text and controls for the main task. Check its rendering cost on the devices your audience uses.

usage-meter-tokens.useWhen: Showing supplied token consumption, limits and remaining allowance.
usage-meter-tokens.avoidWhen: A billing authority or a usage estimate presented as a measured total.
integration: Supply your own records through `catalog`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.

work-index-hover.useWhen: An editorial work index with authentic project previews.
work-index-hover.avoidWhen: Essential project context discoverable only through mouse hover.
integration: Supply your own records through `projects`. Preserve stable keys or IDs when the data contract provides them.

layout-workspace-shell.useWhen: An application page needs one frame for identity, section navigation, a compact page header with actions and several working views, such as a dashboard, settings area or team space.
layout-workspace-shell.avoidWhen: A single card, a marketing page or a modal flow; the shell adds navigation chrome those do not need.
integration: For tabbed apps pass `activeId` and `onNavigate`; links become keyboard tabs (arrows, Home, End) whose `href` `#id` names the panel they control. Without `onNavigate`, links stay real routes or anchors.
Wrap views in `WorkspacePanels` to keep every view mounted so drafts survive a switch; add `fill` inside a fixed-height shell so each view scrolls on its own.

Content can use the shell's tokens (`--ws-surface`, `--ws-line`, `--ws-ink`, `--ws-muted`, `--ws-accent`). Links take an optional 16px `icon` and a `badge`; `railFooter` pins an account or status to the rail.

block-saas-dashboard.useWhen: A SaaS overview needs connected headline measures, a selectable metric trend and the account records behind the numbers.
block-saas-dashboard.avoidWhen: A single metric card or a large analytics warehouse requiring server aggregation and virtualised tables.
integration: Supply `metrics`, `records` and `columns` from the same reporting source. Selecting a KPI or time range updates the shared chart context.
Use `onExport` for your own reporting service, or keep the built-in metric CSV download. Failed callbacks preserve the current view.
Install the four declared components with the block. Each remains available for independent customisation.

block-workspace-settings.useWhen: An account or workspace needs one considered page for its profile, notification choices and role permissions.
block-workspace-settings.avoidWhen: A small single-preference panel or an authorisation service implemented entirely in the browser.
integration: Connect `onSave` to your administration service. Its discriminated payload identifies the section and preserves the underlying component contracts.
Command-S or Control-S saves the section containing keyboard focus. Rejected saves retain the current draft.
Provide consistent roles, permission prerequisites and grants. The server must enforce the resulting access policy.

block-financial-report.useWhen: A financial review needs an intelligible narrative, budget comparison, spend allocation and the underlying cost records in one printable page.
block-financial-report.avoidWhen: Posting accounting transactions, calculating tax obligations or presenting an authoritative ledger without validated source data.
integration: Provide complete `periods` with integer minor-unit amounts and unique line IDs. Invalid records disable export rather than inventing a total.
Every panel follows the selected period. CSV export uses that period; Print report opens a plain, readable print layout.
Use `onExport` to connect a reporting service, or keep the built-in CSV download. Rejected exports preserve the selected context.

block-fashion-workspace.useWhen: A fashion team needs collection performance, a working line plan and launch readiness within the same product workspace.
block-fashion-workspace.avoidWhen: An authoritative inventory or manufacturing system without current catalogue data and reviewed host actions.
integration: Supply one `scopes` record per collection. Its performance records, line budget and launches share a single context.
The block keeps every view mounted so an unfinished line plan survives collection and view changes.
Save and schedule callbacks include the collection ID alongside the underlying typed payload. The offline preview accepts local example changes.

block-people-workspace.useWhen: A people team needs department context, new-hire tasks and leave coverage in one product workspace.
block-people-workspace.avoidWhen: Payroll processing, automatic hiring decisions or leave approvals disconnected from authoritative HR records.
integration: Provide consistent employee IDs across department members, milestones, onboarding and leave records.
The block retains the separate views and their drafts. Each completion or decision carries its department ID and the underlying typed payload.
Connect the callbacks to your HR service. The default export is an offline example; production actions require a supplied host callback.

block-legal-workspace.useWhen: A legal operations team needs matter context, contractual work and requested evidence in one coherent workspace.
block-legal-workspace.avoidWhen: Automatically interpreting obligations, calculating authoritative legal deadlines or treating UI uploads as verified evidence.
integration: Provide related records through `scopes`. Each view stays within its selected matter, and callbacks include the matter ID.
The retained panels preserve unfinished evidence notes when you change matter or view.
The host validates permissions, deadlines, uploaded files and recorded completion. The preview demonstrates local sample handoffs.

block-commerce-workspace.useWhen: A store operations team needs reporting context, order inspection and a reviewed returns workflow in one page.
block-commerce-workspace.avoidWhen: Moving money, reserving inventory or authorising a return solely from frontend state.
integration: Align the records in each `periods` entry. Selecting a measure updates its target comparison, while the order and return views keep the same period context.
Return drafts remain mounted separately for each period and order. The callback includes the period ID and the exact typed return request.
Use `onReturn` to validate and record requests. A returned reference confirms the request; refunds and exchanges remain host operations.

block-saas-landing.useWhen: A SaaS launch needs one considered story from the product introduction through workflow, plan comparison and an actionable request form.
block-saas-landing.avoidWhen: A checkout, authentication service or immediate subscription entitlement implemented only in frontend state.
integration: Replace `plans` and `groups` with your actual offer. The example prices and workflow records are clearly labelled sample data.
Plan CTAs carry their plan ID to the request form. Pending requests lock the plan comparison, and rejected requests retain the email.
Connect `onStart` to your signup or request service. Each anchor reaches a real section, and the default export uses a local offline example.

media-audio-transport.useWhen: Playing music or long-form audio you host, where a waveform scrubber, buffering, speed and volume should feel like a real player, as a cover view or a slim persistent bar.
media-audio-transport.avoidWhen: Short UI sounds, voice recording, or media you lack rights to stream; and very large remote files you can’t precompute peaks for, unless you accept a flat timeline.
integration: Supply a licensed URL in track.src. The waveform is decoded from it, or pass track.peaks (any length, 0–1) to skip decoding; set waveformFromSource={false} to draw a flat timeline instead.
Increment playRequest when someone chooses a track to play; plain next and previous keep the pause state. onNext also runs when a track ends, unless repeat is on.
onPlaybackChange follows the element’s real events, including failures. Start autoplaying previews with defaultMuted; startAt resumes a saved position.

media-track-list.useWhen: A playlist, album or Up Next queue where people scan, play, like and reorder tracks, and the playing row should be obvious at a glance.
media-track-list.avoidWhen: A single now-playing view or a podcast episode page with long descriptions; use the Audio Player, or a list built for long text.
integration: Pass unique track IDs; activeId and playing come from your player. progress (0–1) draws the hairline, and level accepts a number or a per-frame getter such as an AnalyserNode reading.
onSelect plays a row; add onPause so pressing the playing row pauses it. Like, queue and remove are sibling buttons, shown only when you pass their callbacks.
onReorder turns on drag handles and arrow-key moves, and is called once on release with the new ID order. Without artwork, covers are drawn from the album name and match the Audio Player’s.

block-music-workspace.useWhen: Composing a full listening application with discovery, a searchable collection, a shared queue and persistent playback.
block-music-workspace.avoidWhen: Copying a streaming service brand or publishing an audio catalogue without rights to its media and artwork.
integration: Supply MusicTrack records with licensed src URLs. Selection and playback remain distinct and actual media events govern playing state.
Persist queue and liked-state changes through host observers. Retained views keep the collection, search and player position intact.
The offline demo uses fictional releases and original 12-second audio; it begins muted. Production integrations own licensed assets.

collab-message-list.useWhen: A team channel or direct conversation that people read, react to and reply from, where arrivals, unread position and threads matter.
collab-message-list.avoidWhen: Feedback anchored to a document passage (use the Comment Thread) or a one-to-one assistant chat with streaming answers.
integration: Pass messages oldest first with stable IDs and author IDs, plus people with handles so @mentions render. day labels group the list and stick while you scroll.
lastReadId places the New line and opens the list there; posts arriving while someone reads history are counted in a jump pill instead of moving them.
onReaction toggles the signed-in person’s reaction, including kinds a message doesn’t have yet; onReply opens your thread view; mark your own posts status "sending" or "failed" and handle onRetry.

block-team-workspace.useWhen: Composing channels and direct-message rooms with persistent drafts, an asynchronous send contract and retained threads.
block-team-workspace.avoidWhen: Publishing a communication application without supplying its transport, user identity and persistence requirements.
integration: Supply channels, people and initialMessages with stable IDs. onSend returns the server’s authoritative channel-scoped message.
Channel drafts and opened threads remain mounted. A late response never clears text edited during the request.
Reactions and thread interactions are session state in the example; hosts own durable storage and realtime transport.

collab-call-stage.useWhen: The live view of a video meeting in your product: participant tiles from your WebRTC transport, a speaking indicator that follows real audio levels, layouts people switch between, captions and the core media controls.
collab-call-stage.avoidWhen: Showing a meeting that isn’t live, faking presence or speech with animation, or webinars with hundreds of attendees that need paging and a stage/audience split.
integration: Pass each participant’s MediaStream from your transport and a getAudioLevel(id) that reads your AnalyserNode values; it is polled per frame without re-rendering.
Return promises from onMicrophoneChange, onCameraChange and onLeave so controls show pending, and reject with a readable message (permission denied, no device) to keep the old state.
Give the stage a height; tiles scroll inside it. Use CallControls on its own when the controls must stay visible across views.

block-meetings-workspace.useWhen: Composing a working meeting application with linked agenda context, persistent room controls and independently retained notes.
block-meetings-workspace.avoidWhen: Treating an interface block as a conferencing transport or declaring a room joined before the host acknowledges it.
integration: Supply agenda days, participant streams and join/leave callbacks. Keep selected meeting separate from the joined session.
Media callbacks resolve after host state changes succeed; failures preserve the previous control state.
Notes remain scoped by meeting ID. Hosts own storage, permissions and transport; the offline room uses fictional, camera-off participants.

button-shimmer-track.useWhen: The one primary action at the end of a flow kicks off real async work (deploy, publish, send, migrate) and the button itself should show it running, its progress and its outcome.
button-shimmer-track.avoidWhen: Several actions compete on one screen, the action completes instantly, or the moving light would be the only cue that something is available or finished.
integration: Return a promise from onAction and honour its AbortSignal; resolve for success and reject with an error for the retry state.
Pass progress (0–1) when your job reports it, so the light becomes a meter; leave it out for an indeterminate orbit.
Drive status from your store when other UI depends on it, and set it back to idle to start a new run.

cards-prismatic-folder.useWhen: A small, curated set of files deserves to feel like a thing you hand over: a brand kit, a press pack, a client deliverable, a release bundle, where opening the folder is part of the moment.
cards-prismatic-folder.avoidWhen: Large directories, nested folders, bulk selection and file management, or anywhere people need sorting, search and drag-and-drop.
integration: Pass files with stable ids, a short kind, human size and date, and a plain-text preview when you have one; the first three become the folder’s sheets.
Drive status from your fetch (loading, unavailable) and wire onRetry; return a promise from onFileOpen and reject with a readable message on failure.
Give it room: the folder sits beside its list from about 52rem of container width and stacks below that.

navigation-context-rail.useWhen: An app with a handful of top-level areas, each holding its own list of destinations (projects, inbox views, libraries), where people hop between areas and expect each to remember where they were.
navigation-context-rail.avoidWhen: A site with a few flat pages, deep trees that need expand-and-collapse, or navigation that should show the content itself rather than lead to it.
integration: Wrap your page in it as children and give it a height; it docks the list beside the page from 640px and becomes a drawer below.
Map sections and items to your routes with stable ids; return a promise from onValueChange that resolves once the route has loaded, and honour the AbortSignal.
Use badge for unread counts, meta for trailing counts or dates, and disabledReason for locked destinations.

effect-border-tracer.useWhen: A card stands for work in progress (a sync, a build, an agent run, a generating answer) and a light lapping its edge should say “busy” without moving the content.
effect-border-tracer.avoidWhen: Decoration on every card, dense reading surfaces, or as the only sign of status; pair it with a written state.
integration: Bind `enabled` to the real job state; when it turns false the light glides to a stop and rests as a dim glint.
Give the child an opaque background and `border-radius: inherit`, and set `radius` to match it. The halo spills outside the edge, so leave a little room or clip the stage horizontally.
Use `mode="interaction"` to light it only on hover, touch-hold or keyboard focus within. With reduced motion the light parks instead of moving.

input-detent-dial.useWhen: A bounded setting people tune by feel (a level, a gain, a temperature, an intensity) and where seeing the position on an arc matters as much as the number.
input-detent-dial.avoidWhen: Unbounded or very fine-grained quantities, dense forms with many numeric fields, or settings people only ever type.
integration: Bind value and onValueChange to the setting; onValueChange fires on every detent while turning.
Persist in onValueCommit and return a promise: the dial shows Saving, Saved, or a Retry if it rejects, without moving the value.
Pick min, max and step for the domain; pass marks for the labelled positions and set disabledReason when the control is locked.

devtools-icon-workbench.useWhen: An icon picker or icon-set site where people browse, tune size and stroke, check how a glyph is built and copy production SVG or JSX.
devtools-icon-workbench.avoidWhen: Filled or multi-colour icon sets, a single icon field in a form, or picking from thousands of icons without categories.
integration: Pass glyphs as stroke paths on a 24-unit grid (or with their own viewBox) with keywords for search; keep selectedId and onSelect in sync if the choice is saved.
Set size and strokeWidth to your product's defaults; exports use stroke="currentColor" so icons inherit text colour.
Use onCopy to insert into an editor or a host clipboard; when it rejects, the source is selected so people can still copy by hand.

navigation-lens-dock.useWhen: A launcher or workspace switcher with five to ten destinations where recognisable app tiles, unread badges and a playful but precise hover are part of the product’s feel.
navigation-lens-dock.avoidWhen: Deep or text-heavy navigation, more than about ten destinations, or layouts where a bottom dock would cover content people need.
integration: Pass items with stable ids, labels and icons; use tile for the material, badge for counts, running for open apps, separated for system tools and disabledReason for locked ones.
Open destinations in onActivate and return the promise: the dock shows a spinner, aborts superseded opens through the signal, and offers Retry when it rejects. Update value once it resolves.
Set size and magnification for your layout; the dock shrinks, eases the swell and finally scrolls on its own in narrow containers.

hero-signal-workbench.useWhen: A landing page for an audio, DSP, synthesis or data-signal product where letting visitors turn a parameter and watch the result says more than a screenshot.
hero-signal-workbench.avoidWhen: Products with no meaningful signal or parameter story, pages that must stay static for performance budgets, or a hero that needs real audio playback.
integration: Replace the headline, emphasis word, body, actions and note with your product's; keep the headline to two or three short lines.
Set the starting waveform, frequency (Hz) and gain (dB), or control value/onChange to sync the patch with other parts of the page.
The scope animates only while visible and stops drifting under reduced motion; it draws a visual model and makes no audio or network requests.

navigation-stacked-tabs.useWhen: Several documents share one working area and people reorder, close and reopen them while unsaved drafts must survive: editors, IDEs, spreadsheets, design files.
navigation-stacked-tabs.avoidWhen: A short, fixed set of product sections; an ordinary tab bar is easier to scan and has no document lifecycle.
integration: Give each document a stable `id`, a `kind` for its icon and an honest `dirty` flag; bump `revision` when you save so an in-flight close of an older draft is cancelled.
Return promises from `onCloseRequest`, `onRestoreRequest` and `onOrderChange` and honour their AbortSignal; rejecting keeps the tab and its draft and offers Retry.
Treat `items` as authoritative: removing a document retires its tab, its History entry and its retained editor. Change `resetKey` when the workspace or account changes.

layout-split-resizer.useWhen: Two related views share one space and people tune the balance: a query and its results, an editor and its preview, a list and the record it opens.
layout-split-resizer.avoidWhen: Independent page sections that should simply stack and scroll, or panes too dense to stay useful at their minimum width.
integration: Set `minPrimary` and `minSecondary` to the narrowest each pane stays useful; dragging past a minimum resists, then folds the pane into a rail that restores it.
Persist the split from `onValueChange(value, reason)`, which fires once a drag, key or fold settles; 0 and 100 mean a folded pane.
Choose `snapPoints` that match your layouts (for example 33, 50, 67); PageUp and PageDown step between them from the keyboard.
Panes stay mounted when folded, so editors keep drafts and scroll; each pane is its own container for container queries.

media-device-switcher.useWhen: Showing how one page reads on a phone, a tablet and a desktop, with the page itself as the hero: theme galleries, design reviews, template marketplaces and CMS previews.
media-device-switcher.avoidWhen: Testing real devices or browsers, or showing a static screenshot; this renders your live page in a container at the device width, it doesn't emulate an operating system.
integration: Pass the page as `content`. It renders inside a CSS container at the device width, so use container queries (or components built on them); window media queries see the host window, not the device.
Supply your own `presets` (id, label, kind, width, height) and drive `value`, `rotated` and `fit` if the choice lives in your URL or store.
Map your build or fetch state to `status` (loading, empty, error) and pass `onRetry`; the page stays mounted underneath so its state survives.

media-image-contact-sheet.useWhen: Editing a shoot down to its keepers: a photographer or editor scanning a roll or a card of near-identical frames, picking the best of each sequence and rejecting the misses, then handing the picks on.
media-image-contact-sheet.avoidWhen: Browsing a finished gallery, single-image zoom and retouching, or collections without any sequence where a plain grid reads better.
integration: Pass frames in shooting order with stable ids, alt text and src thumbnails (about 600px wide is plenty; the loupe magnifies the same image). Store flags from onFlagsChange as the edit’s source of truth and seed defaultFlags from it.
onSendPicks receives ids in the order they were picked and an AbortSignal; reject to show Try again with every mark kept.
Use status for scans still arriving (loading) or a failed fetch (error with onRetry); an empty frames array shows the empty roll.

media-focus-lightbox.useWhen: A portfolio, case study or product gallery where people open photographs to look closely: a contact sheet of real ratios, a shared-element open, zoom, pan and a filmstrip.
media-focus-lightbox.avoidWhen: Documents, video, a carousel that should autoplay, or images too small to reward zooming.
integration: Pass each image's natural width and height with its src, a descriptive alt and a title; the sheet and the opening flight keep that exact ratio. Captions and a one-line meta (camera, lens, exposure) are optional.

Leave open and value uncontrolled for a gallery page; control them with onOpenChange and onValueChange to deep-link a frame. Without a handler the matching action becomes read-only rather than silently ignored.

media-trim-timeline.useWhen: Cutting a clip out of a recording: a quote from an interview, a podcast highlight, a voice note to share, or a ringtone, where the cut should land in a breath rather than mid-word.
media-trim-timeline.avoidWhen: Multi-track editing, fades and effects, video frame-accurate trimming, or recordings with no waveform data available.
integration: Pass media with duration and peaks (0–1 amplitudes spread evenly over the file, 20–50 a second); compute them once on upload and cache them. Add src for real playback, otherwise the playhead runs silently.
Keep the result of onRangeChange as a draft and save it in onApply(range, signal); reject to show Try again with the range kept. The signal aborts on unmount or a newer save.
Turn snapToPauses off for music, where quiet runs aren’t natural cut points, and raise minLength for formats with a minimum duration.

media-spatial-collection.useWhen: Browsing a small music or media collection where the objects themselves matter: album sleeves in depth with the record sliding out, a tracklist beside it and an equally good list view.
media-spatial-collection.avoidWhen: Playing audio, sorting or filtering hundreds of items, or any collection without artwork worth looking at.
integration: Pass albums with stable ids, square cover URLs, a record label tint and entries whose size is an m:ss duration so the runtime adds up. Missing or failed covers fall back to a typeset sleeve.

Control selectedId and view only if your app must own them; without the matching handler they become read-only. onOpenCollection receives an AbortSignal that a new selection aborts, and a rejection shows its message with a retry.
Use status for loading and unavailable libraries (with error and onRetry) and onCreate for an empty one; reduced motion keeps a static shelf and the full list.

media-transcript-player.useWhen: Podcasts, interviews, lessons or voice notes where people read along with the audio, jump to a word or line, and scrub a waveform of the real recording.
media-transcript-player.avoidWhen: Generating transcripts or captions, long multi-speaker meetings that need speaker diarisation and editing, or video, where captions belong over the picture.
integration: Pass the recording as media (id, title, src, duration hint, speaker, measured peaks) and timed passages; add per-word start times in words when your speech-to-text returns them, otherwise words are spaced by length.

The native audio element is the clock. Persist position with onSeek or onTimeChange (at most 10 Hz), gate seeks with onBeforeSeek, and drive status/error/onRetry from your media host; the transcript stays readable when audio can’t load.

media-compare-grid.useWhen: Choosing between versions of the same image (paper stocks, print proofs, retouches, renders, compression settings) where the difference lives in details you need to zoom into on every version at once.
media-compare-grid.avoidWhen: A single before/after reveal (use a wipe), comparing unrelated images with different framing, or comparing text and numbers rather than pixels.
integration: Pass up to four variants with stable ids, labels and image URLs at the same framing and size; add description and specs for the facts that matter to the decision.

Control the view with value/onValueChange if you need to sync or restore it, and persist finished gestures from onValueCommit. Drive status, error and onRetry from your asset host; loupe and loupeZoom tune the synced magnifier.

portfolio-project-reel.useWhen: A studio, freelancer or agency homepage that leads with a handful of flagship projects, where each cover deserves to be seen large and each case needs a line of story and a few hard numbers.
portfolio-project-reel.avoidWhen: An archive of dozens of projects (use an index or grid), a product carousel in a shop, or anything that should autoplay.
integration: Pass three to eight projects with stable ids. Supply image (and imageAlt) for your own covers; results are { value, label, prefix?, suffix?, decimals? } so the figures can count. Leave href off for work under NDA and the link disappears.
onProjectChange reports the centred project after any scroll, swipe or button press; use it for analytics or to preload that case study. defaultProject picks where the reel starts.
The reel sizes itself from its container, so it works full-bleed or inside a column; give it at least 320px.

media-crop-workbench.useWhen: Framing a photo before it is published or printed: avatars, product shots, editorial images and social crops where the ratio is fixed and the horizon has to be level.
media-crop-workbench.avoidWhen: Retouching, filters or background removal, or batch cropping many images at once without looking at each one.
integration: Pass image with the original's pixel width and height and, if you like, a smaller preview as src; the crop result is measured against the original, so pixels and output are full-resolution.

Store the result from onChange as a draft and save it in onApply(result, signal). Reject the promise to show Try again with the crop intact; the signal aborts when a newer save starts or the editor unmounts.
Customize the presets with aspects ({ key, label, ratio }), using "original" to follow the photo and null for free-form.

media-caption-styler.useWhen: A video or social tool where people set caption type, placement and panel over their own footage and need to see wrapping, safe-area crossings and contrast before they export.
media-caption-styler.avoidWhen: Transcribing speech, translating subtitles, timing captions to audio or rendering them into a video file.
integration: Pass the footage as media (image or video with alt) and set aspectRatio and safeInset to match the real output; the saved snapshot carries both with a 1080 px reference style.

Control caption, style and guide visibility only if your app owns them; without the matching handler each becomes read-only. onSave receives an AbortSignal that any edit aborts, and Copy CSS falls back to a selectable field when the clipboard is blocked.

hero-layout-playground.useWhen: A landing page for a layout, design-system or component product, where letting visitors drag a boundary and watch real content reflow sells the idea better than a screenshot.
hero-layout-playground.avoidWhen: Switching between fixed device presets, emulating a browser, or a hero whose product has nothing to do with responsive layout.
integration: Pass your own component as content; it must respond to its container (container queries or a ResizeObserver), never the viewport. Set breakpoints to the widths where it actually changes layout so the ruler, guides, readout and chips tell the truth.
Leave width uncontrolled for a marketing page; control it with width/onWidthChange only when another part of the page mirrors it. minWidth, maxWidth and the canvas width bound every request.

features-integration-trace.useWhen: Showing what an integration or automation actually does to data: a feature page, onboarding or a run inspector where one real record should visibly change from source payload to the object it creates.
features-integration-trace.avoidWhen: Building or editing workflows (use a node editor), debugging high-volume webhook traffic, or a logo grid of supported apps.
integration: Pass integrations with ordered stages (source, transform, enrich, action) and give each field a stable id across stages; renames, reformatting, additions and drops are computed and drawn for you. Mark the created object’s title and amount with role.
Control the stage with value/onValueChange to sync it with docs or a URL, hook onRun to log replays, and drive status, errorMessage and onRetry when the run comes from your API.

features-shortcut-theatre.useWhen: A landing or feature page for a keyboard-first product (issue trackers, editors, mail, design tools) where pressing the shortcut sells it better than a list of hotkeys.
features-shortcut-theatre.avoidWhen: Documenting every shortcut (use a reference table), registering global hotkeys on a page, or products whose actions aren’t about speed at the keyboard.
integration: Relabel and rebind the four built-in performances through shortcuts: action is one of create, command, done or sidebar; key is what KeyboardEvent.key reports; mod means ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. Swap the content with issues, people, newIssueTitles, product and issuePrefix.

Shortcuts only listen while the card has focus and never while someone types in a field. onAction reports each press for analytics. Turn on autoplay for a hands-off tour; it stops for good on the first interaction and never runs with reduced motion.

features-compare-lenses.useWhen: A feature or product page that has to show how much better one specific workflow gets: each stage of the old way next to the same stage done with your product, with real working times.
features-compare-lenses.avoidWhen: Image before/after reveals, plan or price comparison tables, or claims you can’t back with real timings from customers.
integration: Pass ordered stages, each with a before and after side: the tool where the work happens, a title, working minutes (a working day is eight hours), five or so rows with ok, warn, error or idle states, and a footer. Totals and the readout are computed from minutes.

Name both ways with beforeLabel and afterLabel, start the lens with defaultValue or control it with value/onValueChange (for example to sync copy beside it), and use status, errorMessage and onRetry when the stages come from a CMS.

pricing-usage-calculator.useWhen: Pricing a metered product (API calls, renders, minutes, seats of compute) where buyers need to see how a base fee, an allowance and per-block overage add up at their own volume.
pricing-usage-calculator.avoidWhen: Flat or per-seat plans, final invoices, or billing with tiers that change price per unit (show those with a tiered table instead).
integration: Pass rates in integer minor units: baseMinor, includedUnits, blockUnits, blockPriceMinor and an explicit rounding rule. started-block bills any touched block in full and shows its unused remainder as already paid for; proportional-ceiling bills per unit, rounded up to the cent. Null rates show a not-set-up state.

Control quantity with quantity/onQuantityChange or start it with defaultQuantity. Presets jump the meter with a sweep but call onQuantityChange once. onContinue receives the quantity and exact estimate; return a promise for the pending state and reject it to show a recoverable failure. Drive status for loading and error and pass onRetry to offer a retry.

pricing-seat-simulator.useWhen: Selling a per-seat plan where a team mixes paid and free roles, and buyers should see the bill rebuild as they add people before they reach checkout.
pricing-seat-simulator.avoidWhen: Managing seats on a live subscription (use a seat manager with proration), flat per-plan pricing with no team size, or usage-metered billing.
integration: Pass roles with stable unique IDs, whole minimum/maximum counts and integer minor-unit rates for the full term: monthly per month, annual per year. Free roles (rate 0) draw as outlined seats; duplicate IDs or out-of-bounds counts show an unavailable bill instead of a wrong one.

Control the mix with value/onValueChange or let it run uncontrolled from defaultValue; changing the term never resets counts. onContinue receives the mix and exact estimate; return a promise to show the pending state and reject it to show a recoverable failure. Drive status for loading and error, and pass onRetry to offer a retry.

social-proof-case-ledger.useWhen: A landing or pricing page that needs measured customer outcomes rather than adjectives: several named customers, each with one metric, before and after figures, a period and a quote.
social-proof-case-ledger.avoidWhen: Short testimonials without numbers (a testimonial wall reads better), or a single headline stat, which belongs in a hero.
integration: Pass cases with before, after, unit, period and better ("lower" or "higher"); the change and the median total are computed, and a zero or missing baseline shows “No baseline” instead of a percentage. Logos are drawn as type through mark.style, so no image assets are needed.
Filters are built from each case’s industry. Use filter/onFilterChange to sync them with the URL, onOpenChange to track which quote was read, and href for the full case study.

content-interactive-spec.useWhen: A product page or spec sheet where people want to see what each part of a physical product is and does: a line drawing with numbered callouts, dimensions and a linked specification list.
content-interactive-spec.avoidWhen: Photographic product galleries, CAD-style editing, or diagrams of processes and flows, which want a flowchart or timeline rather than a part-by-part drawing.
integration: Supply `parts` with outline `paths`, an `anchor` for the marker and a `label` point in the drawing units given by `size`; add `scenery` for non-part lines and `dimensions` for overall measurements.
Spec values are text or `{ value, unit }` in mm, m or kg; measured values convert when `units` switches to imperial. A part `dimension` draws when that part is selected.
Selection is controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled from `defaultValue`. Markers and rows are keyboard reachable and arrow keys walk the parts.

cta-project-brief.useWhen: A studio, agency or consultancy contact section where the enquiry itself should sell the service: visitors choose scope, budget and timing and see their brief written back to them before sending.
cta-project-brief.avoidWhen: A one-field newsletter signup, a support form, or a long procurement questionnaire with dozens of fields, which want a simpler form or a multi-page flow.
integration: Pass `services`, `budgets` and `timelines` for your offer; each service has a `phrase` for the letter and a `typical` cost in thousands that drives the scope-against-budget read.
Handle `onSubmit(brief)`: resolve, optionally with `{ reference }`, to stamp it received; throw to keep the draft and show a retry. Nothing is stamped until it resolves.
Seed known details with `defaultValue`, or control the whole brief with `value` and `onValueChange`. Set `currency`, `studio` and `replyNote` to match your studio.

footer-sitemap-atlas.useWhen: A product or documentation site with a few dozen pages, where the footer should help people find a page: a searchable site index with a map plate that gives every page a place.
footer-sitemap-atlas.avoidWhen: A small marketing site with a handful of links, where a wordmark footer says more, or an app where navigation belongs in a command palette.
integration: Supply `groups` of links with real hrefs; add `keywords` for the words people actually search for (jobs, uptime, sdk). Each group becomes a region of the plate and a column of the index.

Pass the current path as `currentHref` to mark the link with `aria-current` and pin it on the plate. Search is local and ignores case and accents; pair `query` with `onQueryChange` to sync it with your router or analytics.
The plate is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the index carries every destination. Turn the plate off with `showMap={false}` in narrow sidebars.

text-optical-weight.useWhen: Showing off a variable typeface on a foundry page, brand guide or type tester, where people should feel the weight axis change real, selectable words.
text-optical-weight.avoidWhen: A static font you can’t vary, a decorative loading animation, or a full type-testing tool with OpenType feature toggles and paragraph settings.
integration: Back the chosen role with your actual face through --font-display, --font-serif or --font-mono, and declare its real weightAxis. Pass opticalAxis only when the face really has opsz; without it no optical control appears. Geist Variable and Geist Mono Variable run 100–900, Instrument Serif is a fixed 400.

Control weight, requested size and optical size together with value/onValueChange, or start from defaultValue. Persist in onValueCommit, which fires once per finished gesture after you accept it. Drive status for loading or an unavailable face and pass onRetry to offer a retry.

text-path-typesetter.useWhen: Letting people set a short phrase along a curve and shape it by hand: badge and label makers, poster or merch editors, a type playground in a design tool.
text-path-typesetter.avoidWhen: Body copy or anything people must read quickly, or a full vector editor with many paths, where a canvas library fits better.
integration: Store the layout from onValueCommit: { path, size, tracking, align }, where path is a cubic Bézier in 0–1 canvas coordinates and size is in units of a 1000-wide canvas, so the same layout renders identically at any width.

Use value and onValueChange to drive it from your own state (onValueChange fires every frame of a drag or morph), text and onTextChange for the phrase, and fontRole for the face. The component measures the path and the set type itself and offers Fit when letters fall off.

text-number-odometer.useWhen: A figure that changes in front of the reader, such as a live total, a balance or a counter, where turning digits make the direction and size of the change legible.
text-number-odometer.avoidWhen: Static numbers that never change after load, dense tables where dozens of figures update at once, or values whose exact reading matters more than the motion.
integration: Render `TextNumberOdometer` inside any text: it inherits font size and colour. Pass `value`, plus `currency`, `locale`, `fractionDigits`, `signDisplay`, `prefix` or `suffix` for Intl-correct formatting.
Set `from={0}` for a first-view count-up. Each new `value` rolls only the digits that changed, up or down, and interrupts cleanly when updates arrive mid-roll.
Set `live` when a screen reader should hear the settled value; the rolling glyphs are hidden from assistive technology. Reduced motion jumps straight to the value.

text-outline-fill.useWhen: A long read or chapter opener where the headline should mark the reader's progress: outlined display type that fills with ink word by word as they scroll.
text-outline-fill.avoidWhen: Short interface labels, buttons or body text, or any headline that has to read at full strength before anyone scrolls.
integration: Pass your reading position as `progress` (0–1), for example the share of the article brought into view. Without it the type fills as it passes through the viewport.
The outline layer is the real heading text, so it is selectable, searchable and read by screen readers; the ink is a decorative copy. Give it one short phrase with deliberate line breaks.
Size it with `fontSize` as a maximum; it measures its widest line and shrinks to fit the container. Reduced motion keeps the fill in step without easing.

bg-fluted-glass.useWhen: A hero, cover or feature panel where an image should read as seen through reeded glass, with headlines, cards or controls on top that must stay sharp.
bg-fluted-glass.avoidWhen: Blurring live page content behind a modal or nav (use backdrop-filter), or behind long-form text without a panel.
integration: Pass your own image as scene.src (a URL, imported asset or data URI) with a short description, and put the real content in children. The filter warps that image only; it does not refract whatever sits behind the element.

Tune with strength (0–32px), flutes (8–40), frost (0–2.5px) and orientation. Values tween live, so they can be bound straight to sliders. On first load the ridges form over 900ms; with reduced motion they appear at once.
Give the wrapper a size with className (min-h-[80vh], aspect-[16/9]). quality="high" doubles the render budget for very large, sharp images; the default keeps the filter cheap.
onSceneStateChange reports loading, ready (with natural size) and error; failed loads show a Retry strip while your content stays usable.

bg-topographic-contours.useWhen: A hero, section or empty state that should feel like terrain, depth or data: outdoor and mapping products, geology, analytics, or any surface where a quiet field of lines suits better than a gradient.
bg-topographic-contours.avoidWhen: An actual map people navigate or measure on, or a layout whose text sits over the whole surface with no room for a scrim.
integration: Wrap your content: <BgTopographicContours className="min-h-dvh">…</BgTopographicContours>. The root needs a height; children render as normal DOM and keep their events.

Pass field={{ columns, rows, values }} to draw your own data (elevation, depth, density, a score). It is upsampled before tracing, so modest grids still draw smooth lines; onProbe returns the field's value under the pointer in its own unit.

drift is the only ambient motion and stops offscreen, in hidden tabs and under reduced motion; set it to 0 for a still surface. Add a scrim behind dense type, as the demo does, so the lines never fight the copy.

pixel-halftone-image.useWhen: Giving people a print-style halftone of their own image, in an editor, a poster or zine maker, or an asset pipeline, with a direct comparison against the original and a file they can keep.
pixel-halftone-image.avoidWhen: A decorative dotted background with no source image, or general photo editing where crops, colour and filters matter more than a screen.
integration: Pass `source` with an id, URL, alt text and title. The pixels are read through a canvas, so remote images must send CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin); data: and blob: URLs always work. Without CORS the stage shows a designed error instead of a blank canvas.
Settings are `{ cell, threshold, angle, shape }`; keep them uncontrolled with `defaultValue` or control them with `value` and `onValueChange` to save presets. Out-of-range values are clamped.

`onExport(result, signal)` receives a PNG Blob repainted at `exportScale` times the on-screen size (longest side capped at 4096px), its dimensions, the source id and the settings. Upload or store it there; throw to show your error. A download link appears in the receipt either way.

Set `ink` for a duotone or risograph look; the chrome stays neutral. The canvas runs only while settings change or the entrance plays, pauses offscreen and renders one static frame with reduced motion.

effect-ink-trail.useWhen: A hero, guestbook, signature or campaign page where leaving a brush mark is the moment, and the page’s own content and buttons should stay usable on top of it.
effect-ink-trail.avoidWhen: Precise drawing or annotation tools that need undo, layers and vector export, or text-heavy pages where a pointer effect would compete with reading.
integration: Wrap your content: `<EffectInkTrail>{hero}</EffectInkTrail>`. Links, buttons, labels and fields inside keep their own pointer events; everything else paints.
Save marks from `onStroke` and replay them with `initialStrokes`; points are in units of the surface’s shorter side from its centre, so a saved signature keeps its shape at any size.

Tune feel with `width`, `lifetimeMs` (0 keeps marks), `maxStrokes` and `mode` (`trail` follows the pointer without pressing). The loop sleeps when idle and offscreen, and reduced motion shows marks without fades.

three-material-inspector.useWhen: Choosing between surface finishes for a part or product by seeing how each takes a studio light, with metalness, roughness and transmission read out beside it.
three-material-inspector.avoidWhen: Showing an actual product (use its real photography or model) or making certified physical claims about a material.
integration: Pass 1 to 8 `materials`, each with id, label, description, #rrggbb colour, metalness 0 to 1, roughness 0.15 to 1 and optional transmission up to 0.8. Name the sample with `title` and `path`.
The view is one value: `{ materialId, azimuth, lightAngle }`. Use `value` and `onValueChange` to control it (throw to refuse a view) and `onValueCommit` to save finished interactions only.

`quality` sets the drawing-buffer budget (480k or 960k pixels, DPR capped at 1.5 or 2). Rendering is on demand, pauses offscreen and disposes on unmount; without WebGL a drawing and the parameters remain.

three-exploded-assembly.useWhen: Explaining how a physical product goes together: an enclosure, a fixture, a kit of parts, with each part numbered against a parts list and the separation under the reader's control.
three-exploded-assembly.avoidWhen: Imported CAD models with hundreds of parts, tolerance analysis or manufacturing sign-off, where a dedicated CAD viewer belongs.
integration: Pass 1 to 12 `parts` in model units: id, label, description, kind (box, cylinder or frame), size, position, an explode vector for full separation, a #rrggbb colour and optional material and metalness. Keep colours neutral unless they mean something.
Set `unit` so dimensions read in real units (`{ label: "mm", perUnit: 40 }` shows 2.5 units as 100 mm). The parts list, toolbar summary and stack height all use it.
The view is one value: `{ selectedId, separation, azimuth }`. Control it with `value` and `onValueChange` (throw to refuse a view) and save finished interactions from `onValueCommit`.
`quality` sets the pixel budget; rendering is on demand, pauses offscreen and disposes on unmount. Without WebGL an isometric drawing and the parts list remain.

input-dual-range.useWhen: Filtering by an interval where the shape of the data matters: price, duration, size or score, with a histogram showing how many results each band holds.
input-dual-range.avoidWhen: A single threshold, where one slider is clearer, or a media timeline that needs playback and scrubbing.
integration: Pass value and onValueChange for a controlled pair, or defaultValue for an uncontrolled one. Query your data in onValueCommit, which fires once per drag, key step or committed field, not on every frame.

histogram is item counts in equal bins from min to max. Recompute it from the other active filters so the lit band and the match count stay honest; omit it (or set showHistogram to false) when you have no distribution.
minimumGap keeps the ends apart in whole steps; collision chooses whether a moving end stops at the gap or pushes its neighbour. Use prefix, suffix, locale and openEnded to format the figures.

input-unit-converter.useWhen: Entering or reading a physical quantity that people think about in different units: lengths for fabrication or shipping, weights in a recipe, temperatures on a device.
input-unit-converter.avoidWhen: Currency conversion with moving rates, or a plain numeric field where everyone uses the same unit.
integration: Store value.base in one base unit and value.unitId for the display. Each unit is { id, label, symbol, factor, offset? } and a figure is base × factor + offset, so switching units only changes unitId and the stored quantity is never rounded.

onValueChange fires on every frame of a drag or fling as well as on taps, keys and typed values; debounce there if you save remotely. Set minBase and maxBase to the real limits so the tape dims past them and typed values outside them are refused with the range.
span sets the physical zoom of the tape in base units; precision caps the decimals shown, and figures that had to round are marked ≈.

input-cron-builder.useWhen: Letting someone set when a recurring job runs (reminders, exports, digests, syncs) and see exactly when it will fire, including across a clock change.
input-cron-builder.avoidWhen: Arbitrary cron syntax such as every 15 minutes, day-of-month rules or several times a day; use a raw expression editor for those.
integration: Store CronSchedule as data: cadence (daily | weekly), time "HH:mm", weekdays 0 (Sunday) to 6, an IANA timeZone and repeatedTime (first | second). cronExpression(schedule) gives the five fields; run them with CRON_TZ set to the zone so the scheduler reads the time locally.

Pass referenceInstant as the current time (new Date().toISOString()) so the ribbon and the upcoming list start from now. nextCronOccurrences(schedule, referenceInstant, count) is exported for server-side previews and uses the same daylight-saving rules: missing local times are skipped, repeated ones follow repeatedTime.

Return the save promise from onValueChange to show Saving and Saved; reject it to keep the draft with an error. In controlled mode, update value once the server accepts; an edit made meanwhile is never overwritten. Change resetKey when switching jobs.
Use status loading while the schedule loads and error with onRetry when the scheduler is unreachable; disabled shows the schedule read only.

input-expression-editor.useWhen: Letting people define a computed column, a pricing rule or a filter as a short formula over known fields, with immediate feedback against real rows.
input-expression-editor.avoidWhen: Writing general-purpose code or long scripts, or when a few dropdowns would express the rule without any syntax to learn.
integration: Describe each field as { id, label, kind: number | text | boolean, format? } and pass a handful of real rows as { id, label, values } so the preview and the field list show true values. Keep ids identifier-shaped (letters, digits, underscores).

Validate on the server with the exported analyzeExpression(formula, fields) and compute with evaluateExpression(formula, values, fields): the same closed grammar the editor uses, with five functions (ROUND, IF, MIN, MAX, ABS) and no eval.

Return the save promise from onValueChange to show Saving and Saved; reject it to keep the draft with an error. Save is only offered for a formula that type-checks. Change resetKey when switching columns.
Use status loading or error while sample rows load; the formula is still visible, and editing resumes when ready.

selects-tree-picker.useWhen: Choosing several items from a hierarchy where whole branches are often wanted at once: teams in an org, regions and stores, folders to sync, permission scopes.
selects-tree-picker.avoidWhen: A flat list of options, where a listbox or multi-select is simpler, or browsing and opening files, where a file explorer fits.
integration: Pass `nodes` as a tree of `{ id, label, count?, members?, children?, disabled?, disabledReason? }`. Ids must be unique; `count` feeds the running total and `members` the initials on each row. A disabled node locks everything under it and shows its reason.

The value is leaf ids only. Keep it uncontrolled with `defaultValue`, or control it with `value` and `onValueChange`, which receives the full selection in tree order. Checking a group adds every selectable leaf under it, including ones a search is hiding.

Set `itemNouns` and `countNouns` for your domain ("store"/"stores", "seat"/"seats"). Turn `summarize` off when every chosen leaf should keep its own chip. Use `status` with `onRetry` while the hierarchy loads from your API.

date-range-calendar.useWhen: Choosing a start and end date where the length matters: stays, rentals, leave requests or report periods, with booked days and optional per-day prices visible as you pick.
date-range-calendar.avoidWhen: Picking a single date or a time slot within a day, or a range that only needs two text fields in a dense filter bar.
integration: Pass `value`/`onValueChange` (or `defaultValue`) as `{ start, end }` YYYY-MM-DD strings. All arithmetic is whole UTC days, so a date never shifts across timezones.

Set `unit` to `nights` for stays (end − start; a booked day can still be the check-out) or `days` for inclusive ranges. Bound it with `minDate`, `maxDate`, `minLength`, `maxLength` and `unavailableDates`.

Supply `rates` to show prices under each day and a running total. `onApply` adds a primary button; return a promise to show the pending state, reject to show the retry state with the selection kept. Pass `today` from your server so the today marker and default presets agree with it.

date-timezone-overlap.useWhen: Finding a meeting time for a distributed team: you need to see everyone’s working hours side by side and read what a proposed time means locally for each person.
date-timezone-overlap.avoidWhen: Booking against real calendar availability or rooms (use a booking or slot picker fed by free/busy data), or a single person converting one time between two zones.
integration: Pass `people` as `{ id, name, city, timeZone, start, end, days? }` with IANA zones and local HH:mm hours; offsets and daylight saving come from the browser’s Intl data, and an end before the start runs past midnight.
Set `date` and `anchorZone` to the organiser’s day and zone. Read the meeting from `onSlotChange` as `{ start, end, durationMinutes, participantIds }` with ISO instants.

`onPropose` adds the primary action; return a promise for the pending state and reject to show retry with the slot kept. Working hours are not availability: check calendars on your side before sending invites.

forms-branching-survey.useWhen: Intake briefs, onboarding and qualification flows where earlier answers decide which questions come next, and people benefit from seeing where the path goes and what they skipped.
forms-branching-survey.avoidWhen: Short fixed forms that fit on one screen, or long data entry with many fields per step, where a settings panel or a stepped form reads faster.
integration: Describe `questions` as data: `kind: "choice"` with options (`label`, `description`, and a `preview` node or a `figure`) or `kind: "text"`. Add `showWhen: { questionId, equals }` to branch on an earlier answer.
Save drafts from `onAnswersChange`; it includes answers on branches no longer taken so switching back restores them. Resume with `defaultAnswers` and `defaultQuestionId`.
`onSubmit` receives `{ formId, questionIds, answers }` for the path taken only. Return a promise for the sending state; reject to keep every answer and show retry.

auth-recovery-codes.useWhen: The step after someone turns on two-factor authentication, or a settings page where they view, export and replace their recovery codes.
auth-recovery-codes.avoidWhen: One-time passcode entry at sign-in (use an OTP field), or any flow where the browser would have to generate the secrets itself.
integration: Pass the codes your server issued as `codes` ({ code, usedAt? }), plus `account`, `product` and `generatedAt`. Used codes stay listed and struck through but never reach the clipboard, the file or the printer.
Copy, Download and Print work out of the box. Supply `onDownload` or `onPrint` to log or route exports yourself; reject to show the failed state. Never log the codes themselves.

`onConfirm` runs when the user ticks the box and presses the button; return a promise and reject to keep them on the step with an error. `onRegenerate` adds a confirmed Generate new codes action that should invalidate the old set server-side and resolve with the new one.

forms-draft-rescue.useWhen: Someone returns to a form and a local autosave differs from a newer version saved elsewhere, and they should choose per field what survives before anything is written.
forms-draft-rescue.avoidWhen: Version history across many revisions, or line-level merging of long documents; a version timeline or branch compare reads those better.
integration: Pass the form's `fields` and two versions, `draft` (from local storage or IndexedDB) and `latest` (from the server), each with an id, author, display time, optional origin and `values`. Only fields whose values differ get a picker; a missing key is treated as different from an empty string.
Choices are uncontrolled by default (`defaultSource` decides the starting side) or controlled with `choices` and `onChoicesChange`. Nothing persists until Restore.

`onResolve(resolution, signal)` receives both version ids, one decision per differing field and the merged values for every field. Save against `latestVersionId` so a third concurrent edit is caught, honour the `AbortSignal` (Cancel, unmount or new versions abort it) and throw to show your error message with every choice kept.
Clear the local draft in `onDiscard` and after a successful resolve. Use `status="loading"` while fetching the server copy and `status="error"` with `onRetry` when it fails.

chart-sunburst-explorer.useWhen: Exploring a deep hierarchy where the share of each part matters at every level: bundle sizes, disk usage, time or budget by team and project.
chart-sunburst-explorer.avoidWhen: Flat lists of categories, or comparisons where reading exact differences matters more than part-to-whole (a sorted bar chart reads better).
integration: Pass `data` as { name, value?, children? }. Leaves carry the value and groups sum their children, so there is never a second total to reconcile. Zero-value branches are dropped.
Use `format="bytes"` for file sizes or `format="number"` with `unit` for anything else, and `rings` to trade depth for legibility (3 suits most screens).

`onDrill(path)` reports the names from the root to the level in focus; use it to sync a detail panel or the URL. The list beside the chart is the keyboard path, so keep `showList` on unless another table covers the same data.

chart-sankey-paths.useWhen: Showing how a total splits and recombines across two or three stages, such as acquisition source to first action to outcome, and letting people trace one category’s direct flows.
chart-sankey-paths.avoidWhen: Flows with cycles or links that skip a stage, more than about a dozen categories per column, or a single step-by-step funnel, which a funnel chart reads faster.
integration: Pass `nodes` as { id, label, column } in the top-to-bottom order you want, and flows as { id, source, target, value } between neighbouring columns. Links that skip a column or reference unknown ids are left out of the diagram.
Give `periods` to compare months or cohorts; nodes keep their slots so ribbons and bars morph instead of reshuffling. With a single period, pass `links` instead.
Tracing lights only flows that touch the chosen category. Read it from `onSelectionChange` to filter a table, or control `selection`. Hovering a ribbon shows its share of both ends.
Below 640px the labels move into a grid under the diagram. Use `status` and `onRetry` for loading and failed queries; keep `unit` in step with your noun.

chart-box-distribution.useWhen: Comparing the spread of a measure across a handful of groups, such as latency by region or build time by pipeline, and asking how much of each clears a limit you can drag.
chart-box-distribution.avoidWhen: Showing a single average, a trend over time, or groups with only a few observations each, where a dot plot or a plain table is more honest.
integration: Pass `groups` as { id, label, detail?, values } with raw observations, not pre-computed percentiles. Quartiles use linear interpolation and whiskers reach the furthest values inside 1.5 × IQR; the axis ends just past the slowest p99 and values beyond it are counted at the row’s edge.

Set `defaultThreshold` and `target` (0–1) to mirror your SLO, and persist changes from `onThresholdChange`, or control `threshold` yourself. Rows under target are flagged with an icon as well as colour.
Use `sort` / `onSortChange` to keep the order in sync with a table elsewhere. `showSamples` draws every observation; keep each group to a few hundred values or pass a sample for very large sets.
The limit handle is a slider: arrows move a fiftieth of an axis step, Shift moves five times that. Use `status` and `onRetry` for loading and failed fetches.

chart-calendar-heatmap.useWhen: Showing a year of daily activity at a glance, such as deploys, orders, workouts or support tickets, where weekly rhythm, quiet spells and peak days matter more than exact values.
chart-calendar-heatmap.avoidWhen: Comparing a few series, reading precise daily values, or data with fewer than a couple of months, where a bar or line chart reads faster.
integration: Pass `days` as { date, value } with ISO dates. Use `value: null` for days that weren’t measured; they render hatched and are left out of totals, streaks and averages instead of counting as zero.

Every year present in the data gets a tab. Control it with `year` and `onYearChange`, or set `defaultYear`. Days after the latest record draw as dashed outlines so a partial year still reads as a year.
Use `onSelectDate` to open a day’s detail elsewhere, or control `selectedDate`. Levels come from the quartiles of non-zero days, so a single spike doesn’t wash out the rest of the year.
Name the unit with `unit` ({ one, other }) and set `weekStart` for your locale. The accent tops a four-step ramp mixed in OKLab; pick a hue that stays distinct from your status colours.

chart-scatter-brush.useWhen: Finding and acting on a cluster of records in two measures at once, such as slow pages, expensive accounts or outlier queries, by dragging a box over them.
chart-scatter-brush.avoidWhen: Showing a trend over time, comparing a handful of categories, or plotting thousands of points where a density view or hexbin reads better.
integration: Pass `datasets` as one or more views of the same records ({ id, label, x, y }). Keep ids stable across views: points with the same id travel between them on one shared scale.
Describe each measure with `x` and `y` ({ label, unit, decimals, limit }). A limit draws a dashed guide and tints the passing quadrant; the ranked list sorts by y, highest first.
Read selections from `onBrushChange(brush, selected)` to filter a table or start a bulk action, or control `brush` yourself. Brushes are in data units, so they survive a dataset switch.

Mouse and pen brush by dragging; touch keeps page scroll and taps read the nearest point, so add `presets` for the regions people ask about most. Use `status` and `onRetry` for loading and failed fetches.

chart-funnel-dots.useWhen: Showing how many people make it through each step of a signup, checkout or onboarding flow, and how many drop at each step, as countable dots rather than a bar.
chart-funnel-dots.avoidWhen: Flows with branches or loops, steps measured on different cohorts, or very small counts where a plain table with percentages reads better.
integration: Pass `stages` in order and `segments` as { key, label, counts } where counts[i] belongs to stages[i]. Counts are aggregates per step; the chart doesn’t assume the same individuals at every step.

One people-per-dot weight is shared by every segment, picked from `maxDots` and the largest count, so switching segments compares honestly. The last dot of a step is a wedge for the remainder rather than a rounded whole.

Read the chosen step from `onSelect` to drive a detail panel, or control `selected`. The headline shows that step’s share of step 1; each row shows the share kept from the step before and how many dropped.
