Keep `unit` in step with your noun (visitors, orders, seats). Use `status` and `onRetry` for loading and failed queries.

data-pivot-configurator.useWhen: Letting people slice a modest dataset two ways at once, such as revenue by region and quarter, compare cells at a glance and open any cell to see the records behind it.
data-pivot-configurator.avoidWhen: Millions of rows that need server-side aggregation, or a fixed report whose grouping never changes; a plain chart or table reads faster.
integration: Describe `fields` as dimensions (with an `order` for their values) and measures (with a `format`). Pass the raw `records`; counts, sums and averages are computed locally, and an average is always taken over the records, not over group averages.

Control the grouping with `value` and `onChange`, or start uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. `columns: null` collapses the matrix to one total column. Choosing the other axis's field swaps the axes rather than duplicating one.
Use `onCellSelect` to open the records behind a cell in your own drawer or list; the built-in inspector shows the six largest. Cells are buttons with arrow-key navigation.
Keep matrices small enough to read (four to six values per axis). Turn off `heatmap` when the values aren't comparable, and set `disabled` for read-only dashboards where cells should still open.

data-column-workbench.useWhen: Letting people rearrange a dense operational table in place: drag columns into a new order, freeze the identifying ones on the left, hide the noise and set widths.
data-column-workbench.avoidWhen: Choosing which records to show (that is filtering) or editing cell values; this changes the view of a table, not its data.
integration: Pass `columns` and `rows`; each row's `cells` is keyed by column id and rendered as text, mono, right-aligned numbers or a status with a dot from `tones`. Mark identifier columns `required` so they can't be hidden.

Store the arrangement from `onChange(value, change)`: an ordered `{ id, visible, pinned, width }` array, one entry per column. Drags and resizes report once, on release, so it is safe to save each change to a saved view.
Use `value` to restore a saved layout or `defaultValue` to start uncontrolled. Unknown ids are dropped and missing columns are appended, so a layout saved before you add a column still loads.

Every action has a keyboard path: grips move with the arrow keys, Home and End, and resize handles take arrow keys. Set `disabled` for viewers who may read but not rearrange, and `density="compact"` for long tables.

data-bulk-action-review.useWhen: Running one action over many records where the scope must be seen before it is confirmed, some records can't take the action, and some may fail.
data-bulk-action-review.avoidWhen: A single-record action, or a reversible bulk edit where an undo toast is kinder than a review step.
integration: Pass `records` with `heldReason` on any the action can't touch (an owner, a directory-managed account); they join a held-back pile instead of the action. Give each an `impact` line so the review says exactly what happens to it.
Control `selectedIds` with `onSelectionChange`. The array keeps pick order, which is the stack order. Nothing is selected implicitly; select-all is an explicit checkbox.

`onApply(ids)` receives only the eligible ids and resolves with `{ id, ok, message? }` per record. Failed records stay with their message; rejecting means nothing ran and the review stays open. The scope is frozen at review time, so you can remove finished rows from `records` as soon as the request returns.

Word the action with `action` and `noun`, and use `summarize` for the consequence that matters (seats freed, refund total). Retry reopens a review of just the failures; `onDone(failedIds)` fires when the receipt is dismissed.

data-filter-history.useWhen: Letting people rewind a filtered table through its saved filter states, see exactly which rows each state brings back or drops, and restore one deliberately.
data-filter-history.avoidWhen: Building a filter from scratch, or keeping a long audit log of every edit; this shows a handful of saved states, not a version-control system.
integration: Pass `fields`, `records` and `history` (oldest first). Each snapshot is a full rule set `{ fieldId, operator, value }` with `is`, `is_not`, `contains`, `gte` and `lte`. Counts and rows are computed locally from the records you pass, so send the same rows the live table shows.

Control the live rules with `value` and `onValueChange(rules, snapshotId)`, or start uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. Scrubbing only changes the preview; the host's rules change only when someone presses Restore, and the callback receives a copy.
Add `onRename(id, name)` to enable inline naming. Return a promise for a pending state; reject to keep the draft open with an error, and update `history` with the new name when it succeeds.

Set `defaultSnapshotId` to open on a past state, `showDiff={false}` to hide live rows a snapshot would drop, and `disabled` for read-only viewers who can still scrub. Use `recordLabel` and `noun` to rename the first column and the count for your data.

editor-layer-stack.useWhen: A design or publishing tool where people reorder, hide, lock and fade the layers of a composed artwork and need to see the stack change as they drag.
editor-layer-stack.avoidWhen: Nested scene graphs with deep groups and masks, or lists whose items have no visual to restack, where a plain sortable list fits better.
integration: Pass `value` and `onValueChange` (or `defaultValue`), ordered top first. Each layer has id, name, kind, visible, locked and optional opacity. Every edit sends the full stack; reject the promise with an Error to roll back and show its message.

Give each layer a `render` that fills the artboard and is sized in cqw/cqh: the same node draws the artboard and the row thumbnail. Add `bounds` (fractions of the artboard) for the selection frame, and set `aspect` to the document's width over height.
Selection is separate: `selectedId` and `onSelectedIdChange`, or `defaultSelectedId`. Clicking painted artwork selects the topmost layer there.
`defaultExploded` starts in the 3D view. Locked layers keep their slot; `disabled` makes the panel read-only.

editor-color-token-studio.useWhen: Tuning a design system's semantic colours against the screen they will actually paint, with WCAG contrast for every reading pair updating as you drag.
editor-color-token-studio.avoidWhen: Generating a decorative palette from scratch, or certifying a whole product's accessibility from a handful of token pairs.
integration: Pass `value` and `onValueChange` (or `defaultValue`). Token ids become CSS variables, so keep them CSS-safe (`ink`, `surface-raised`). Apply sends the full palette; reject the promise with an Error to show its message and keep every draft.
Pass your own `specimen`: any JSX that reads `var(--<id>)`. Add `data-token="ink"` to make an element pickable and `data-pair="body"` to underline it when that pair fails AA.

Describe what must stay readable in `pairs` (foreground, background, font size and weight). Large text (24px, or 18.66px at 700) needs 3:1, everything else 4.5:1. Translucent tokens composite over `canvasColor` before measuring.
Copy CSS exports only applied tokens, scoped to `scopeSelector`. Use `disabled` for read-only review.

editor-spacing-inspector.useWhen: Letting designers or builders tune an auto-layout frame's padding, gap, direction and alignment by direct manipulation, with the measured result and its CSS beside it.
editor-spacing-inspector.avoidWhen: A whole-page layout builder, grid or constraint editing, or measuring arbitrary elements on a live website.
integration: Pass the frame's children as layers ({ id, name, content }). Each is rendered inside the frame and measured from the real layout, so hover boxes and the size tag are true; give text layers a width so the frame hugs predictably.

Seed defaultValue with the frame's current spacing ({ direction, align, gap, padding }) and persist from onChange, which fires once per committed value. Padding runs 0–96px and gap 0–64px; snapping to the 4px grid is on by default and can be turned off in the panel.
Use frameClassName for the artwork's own surface and accent for the redline colour. spacingCss(value) returns the same declarations the readout shows if you need them elsewhere.

editor-branch-compare.useWhen: Merging two versions of a written document, such as a copy edit against the live page or a translation pass against the source, where someone chooses change by change and wants to read the merged result before saving.
editor-branch-compare.avoidWhen: Source-code merges with line-level conflicts, three-way merges that need a common ancestor, or reviewing a single version's history (use a version restore instead).
integration: Describe the document as ordered blocks with each branch's text: { id, kind, label?, current?, incoming? }. Matching text reads as unchanged; leave a side out for a block that was added or removed. Give changed blocks a short label for the merge path.
Name both branches with { name, author, updated }. Pass defaultChoices to carry over decisions already made; Merge stays disabled until every change has a side.

onMerge receives { choices, blocks } with the merged document in order. Persist it and resolve; reject with an Error to show its message, and every choice stays for a retry. diffWords is exported if you mark the same changes elsewhere.

editor-asset-license-sheet.useWhen: Checking whether a licensed photo, illustration or commission can run in each placement of a campaign, with its credit line and term in view, before adding it to the project or asking the rights holder for more.
editor-asset-license-sheet.avoidWhen: Browsing or searching a large asset library, negotiating licence terms, or legal review of contract wording.
integration: Describe the project with its dates and planned placements; each placement's aspect is the crop drawn on the asset. Pass each asset's licence facts (holder, licence, territory, reference, term, the placement ids it covers, credit, restrictions) and its media, usually an of your file sized to fill.

Statuses come from your data alone: a placement is cleared when the asset covers it and the term lasts the whole campaign, flagged when the term ends early, and not licensed otherwise. licenceStatus is exported so the rest of your app agrees.

onAdd fires when every ticked placement is cleared; onRequest fires otherwise, with request.blocked naming each placement and why. Persist and resolve, or reject with an Error to show its message; ticks are kept per asset.

editor-storyboard-strip.useWhen: Planning a short film, ad or product video as a sequence of shots, where people reorder shots by drag, trim their lengths and need the cut to land on a target duration.
editor-storyboard-strip.avoidWhen: Frame-accurate editing of real footage, multi-track timelines with audio, or slide decks where items have no duration.
integration: Supply scenes as { id, title, notes, duration, shot, tone, thumbnail }. Pass a real frame URL as thumbnail when you have one; otherwise the board is drawn from the shot type and its two tone colours.
Durations snap to half seconds between 0.5 and 20. Set targetDuration to the length the cut must hit; the meter and readout show the time to spare or the overrun.
onScenesChange receives the full ordered list after each finished change: a drag dropped, an Earlier or Later move, a trim released or a stepper press. Store it as the new order and lengths.

editor-keyframe-track.useWhen: Editing a short UI or motion-design animation by keyframes, where people scrub a playhead, watch a live preview and drag keys in time and value on a curve.
editor-keyframe-track.avoidWhen: Long video timelines with clips and audio, physics or spring authoring, or animations defined entirely in code with no visual tuning.
integration: Give tracks as { id, label, unit, min, max, step, keys } with keys in frame order; each key's ease (linear, ease or hold) shapes the segment that leaves it. Keys never cross or share a frame.

renderPreview(values) receives the current value of every track by id; draw your own component with them. valueAt(track, frame) is exported so your runtime and tests evaluate tracks exactly as the editor does.
onChange(tracks) fires after finished edits only (a drag released, a stepper commit, a key added, re-eased or deleted), so it is safe to persist or push to an undo stack.

editor-version-restore.useWhen: Letting writers browse the saved versions of a document, compare any version with the live text word by word, and restore all of it or only chosen blocks with an undo.
editor-version-restore.avoidWhen: Code review diffs, merge conflict resolution between branches, or audit logs where versions are read but never restored.
integration: Describe the document as ordered blocks ({ id, kind, label }) and give each version text per block id. A block missing from a version reads as not in that version and cannot be restored on its own.
Pass versions newest first. Name the milestones (Copy edit, Legal review) and leave autosaves unnamed; the timeline and the grouped list are built from day and time.

onRestore receives { versionId, blockIds, content }. Persist it and resolve; the component updates the live text, adds a Before restore entry and offers Undo, which calls onUndo with the same request. Reject with an Error to show its message; the ticked blocks stay ticked.

editor-export-preset.useWhen: Exporting a frame, card or layer from a design or content tool, where people pick an artboard size, format, scale and quality and want to see the result and its file size before writing it.
editor-export-preset.avoidWhen: Batch exports of many assets at once, server-side render queues, or a plain download button with no settings to choose.
integration: Pass your own artwork and its background as React nodes. The frame is a size container, so size the artwork in cqw, cqh and cqmin and it reflows to every artboard; the background fades out for transparent exports.

Supply presets as { id, label, width, height, note } and restrict formats to the ones your renderer writes. estimateExportBytes and formatBytes are exported if you show the same figure elsewhere; replace them with your encoder's real numbers when you have them.

onExport receives { presetId, width, height, scale, format, quality, transparent, fileName, estimatedBytes } with the scale already applied. Resolve when the file is written; reject with an Error whose message the panel shows, and every setting stays as it was for a retry.

editor-font-pairing.useWhen: Choosing the heading and body faces, scale ratio, base size and leading for a brand or product type system, judged on a real page of copy rather than on swatches.
editor-font-pairing.avoidWhen: A font marketplace or loader, a rich-text toolbar for styling one document, or a full design-token manager covering colour and spacing too.
integration: Pass the faces you have loaded as fonts: use role (display, serif, sans, mono) for the library's font roles or family with a CSS font-family stack for your own. List only the weights each face ships; the weight control follows them.

Give presets for your house pairings and set defaultPresetId (or defaultValue) to the pairing already live, so the footer can say what has changed. Replace specimen with copy from your own product: the measure ruler counts real characters per line.

onApply receives the pairing, every scale step in px and a CSS variables block (also available from the exported pairingCss and typeScale). Persist it and resolve; reject with an Error to show its message, and the draft stays for a retry.

ai-context-budget.useWhen: Letting someone choose which files, threads and saved pages an assistant reads, with the cost of each shown against the model’s context window and an answer reserve.
ai-context-budget.avoidWhen: A single fixed prompt with nothing to choose, or billing and usage reporting across many requests, where a usage chart reads better.
integration: Pass sources with counts from your own tokenizer; use tokens: null while a source is still being counted, and required: true for instructions that always travel. relevance (0–1) orders what Trim to fit drops first.

Hold the included ids in your state with value and onValueChange, and attach the context in onConfirm(ids, total). Return a promise to show pending; a rejection keeps the selection and shows its message.

ai-answer-compare.useWhen: Showing two model answers to the same prompt so a person can read them side by side, see where they disagree and record which one they prefer: evals, model pickers, A/B tests of prompts.
ai-answer-compare.avoidWhen: A single answer with sources (use an inline-citations or search-answer view), or comparing more than two outputs at once, where a ranked list reads better.
integration: Write each answer as paragraphs of { text, claim?, cite? } parts. Give the same claim key to spans that make the same point in both answers; keys only one answer uses become the highlighted differences. cite ids point into sources, numbered in order.

Record the vote in onSubmit({ choice, reasons }) and return a promise; a rejection keeps the draft and shows its message. Keep blind on to hide the model names until the vote lands, and use status: "loading" | "error" with onRetry for answers that are still streaming or failed.

ai-structured-output.useWhen: Showing a model extract structured data live: JSON streams into a code pane while a schema rail validates each field the moment it closes and flags what failed and why.
ai-structured-output.avoidWhen: Plain chat answers or prose, where streaming text reads better, or a form the user fills in themselves rather than reviewing what a model produced.
integration: Pass the growing JSON as `text` on every chunk with `status` (streaming, done, stopped, error). Partial JSON is expected: each value opens at its first character and closes at its last.
Describe the output in `schema`: path, label, type, required, options, pattern and minItems, plus `check(value, get)` for rules across fields such as totals that must add up.

Wire `onRepair(issues)` to ask the model for the failing fields and list their paths in `repairing` while it rewrites them in `text`; omit it and no repair buttons render. `onStop`, `onRegenerate` and `onCopy` are optional.

agents-dependency-board.useWhen: Showing an agent's plan as tasks with dependencies, where people need to see what is blocking the finish and act on it: retry a failed task, start a ready one, stop a running one.
agents-dependency-board.avoidWhen: A short linear plan with no branches, where an ordered step list is clearer, or a general-purpose node editor where people draw the graph themselves.
integration: Supply tasks with `dependsOn` ids, an `estimate` in minutes and the live `status` (and `progress` while running). The critical path and the finish estimate are recomputed from the work left on every update, so a failed task can become the bottleneck.

Handle `onAction(task, action)` for start, retry and stop. Return a promise: the button shows progress while it is pending, and a rejection's message appears under it so the person can try again. Update `tasks` when the runner reports the new status.

Unknown dependency ids and loops are reported under the graph and left out of it rather than breaking the layout. `layout="auto"` switches from columns to rows when the card is too narrow for readable cards.

agents-run-replay.useWhen: Reviewing a finished agent run step by step: scrubbing to the moment a tool call failed, watching the transcript rebuild as the playhead moves and seeing which files and tests had changed by then.
agents-run-replay.avoidWhen: Watching a run live, or comparing span timings and costs across a whole run, where a tracing waterfall reads faster than a replay.
integration: Map each recorded prompt, thinking span, tool call and reply to an event with `at` and `duration` in ms from the start of the run. Add `files` and `tests` where an event changed files or reported a test result, and the state panel folds them in as the playhead passes.

Leave the playhead uncontrolled for a standalone viewer, or pair `time` with `onTimeChange` to keep it in step with another view. `onEventChange` reports the event under the playhead, for a details pane or a deep link.
Playback only moves the playhead; it never reruns anything. It pauses when the card is off screen or the tab is hidden, and `autoPlay` never starts it with reduced motion.

agents-budget-guard.useWhen: An agent run with spend, token or time limits that should pause before a step that would cross or approach one, and ask a person to approve, raise the cap or stop.
agents-budget-guard.avoidWhen: Showing usage over a billing cycle with no decision to make; a usage meter suits that better. For permission to run a specific command or edit, use an approval gate.
integration: Pass each limit as { id, label, kind, used, next, cap } where next is your estimate for the paused step in the same unit. The guard compares used + next with the cap; it never adds the estimate to the cap or hides an overrun.

Handle onDecision: approve resumes once, raise carries the new money cap in decision.cap, stop ends the run. Return a promise so the button shows progress, and reject it if your orchestrator refuses; the card stays open with the person's choice and drafted cap intact.

Pass history (money per finished step) to show the spend-per-step strip, raiseBy for the offered increments, and status to reset or settle the card from outside. Y, R and S answer while the card has focus; use autoFocus when it appears mid-task.

devtools-release-compare.useWhen: A deploy or release screen where someone decides whether a candidate (or an older release) should replace what's live, and needs the metric changes, risky files and diffs in one place.
devtools-release-compare.avoidWhen: Reviewing a single pull request line by line, or showing deployment history over time; use a diff viewer or a timeline instead.
integration: Pass the live release as base and one ReleaseComparison per candidate: { target, metrics, files, risks }. Metrics carry base, target, unit and better (lower | higher) so deltas are coloured by whether they are good news. A target older than the base is treated as a rollback.

Flag files with risk high or medium (migrations, auth, config); with requireReview each must be marked viewed before the deploy unlocks. Supply unified-diff text as patch; parsePatch and riskScore are exported for server-side use.

onDeploy receives { base, target, direction, riskScore, reviewed }. Return the promise from your deploy API to show progress, and reject to keep the review with an error. Use value and onValueChange to drive the target from the URL.
Use status loading or error while comparisons load; nothing is deployed from those states.

devtools-request-replay.useWhen: Debugging a request that failed in production or staging: edit what was sent, send it again and see exactly how the status, timing and response body changed.
devtools-request-replay.avoidWhen: Documenting an endpoint for first-time use, where an API playground with snippets fits, or browsing a stream of incoming events, where a webhook inspector fits.
integration: Pass `capture` from your request log: id, capture time, source, the request (method, URL, header rows with stable ids, body text) and the response it got (status, statusText, header pairs, body, durationMs). Mask secrets in header values before they reach the browser.

`onReplay(request, signal)` does the real call: you own networking, authentication and CORS, so route it through your backend when the target isn't reachable from the browser. Return the status, headers, body text and a measured `durationMs`; leave it out and the component times the call. Honour the `AbortSignal` (Cancel and Escape abort it) and throw to record a failed run.
Seed `defaultRuns` and `defaultDraft` to restore a session; `onRequestChange` observes edits if you want to persist the draft. JSON bodies are validated before sending when Content-Type is JSON.

devtools-schema-migration.useWhen: An internal tool or developer platform where engineers review and run database migrations: see the steps, their locks and the schema diff, dry-run, then apply.
devtools-schema-migration.avoidWhen: Read-only schema documentation, or ad-hoc SQL consoles where there is no plan to review (use a query editor instead).
integration: Pass `migration` with the target `table` (columns and indexes marked added, removed or changed) and ordered `steps` carrying their SQL, lock level, row and time estimates, and the column or index names they `touches`.

Wire `onDryRun` to run the plan inside a transaction that rolls back and `onApply` to run it for real. Both resolve with { steps: [{ id, rows, ms, error?, hint? }] }; the component plays the result back, stops at the first error and keeps Apply locked until a dry run passes.
Execute the SQL on your server, never in the browser. Without handlers, a sample runner answers from the estimates; `outcome="lock-timeout"` previews the failure state.

devtools-incident-timeline.useWhen: Replaying an outage after the fact: one view of a key metric, severity changes and every alert, deploy, page and rollback, with a playhead to scrub through it.
devtools-incident-timeline.avoidWhen: Live monitoring dashboards that stream new data every second, or incidents with no time series to draw (use a plain activity feed).
integration: Pass `incident` (id, title, service, startedAt), `events` with ISO times and a kind of deploy, alert, severity, page, note, mitigation or resolve, and `metric` samples at a steady interval. Severity events carry `level` 1 to 3 and drive the severity track; a resolve event ends it.

Status, duration, time to detect, time to mitigate, peak and minutes over the `threshold` are computed from the data, so keep timestamps accurate. Use `timeFormat="relative"` for post-mortems that talk in T+ offsets, and `timeZone` for the responders' clock.
`onSeek(at, event)` fires when the playhead settles; use it to sync a log search or a trace view to the moment under the playhead.

mobile-mood-map.useWhen: A wellbeing or journaling app needs a quick, expressive self-reported check-in: people place how they feel on an energy × pleasantness map and log it against their day.
mobile-mood-map.avoidWhen: You need clinical scales (PHQ-9, GAD-7), free-text sentiment detection, or a mood picker so small that a row of chips would do.
integration: Supply your own `feelings` with pleasantness and energy from −1 to 1; the colour of each is blended from the four `colors`, so keep those as your brand's data palette.

Pass today's earlier check-ins as `log` and the current time as `nowMinute`; `onSave` receives { feeling, note, minute } with an AbortSignal and should reject on failure so the retry state appears with the note intact.
Control the selection with `value` and `onValueChange` to sync it with a store; the callback fires when a drag settles, not on every frame.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify the drag, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-habit-grid.useWhen: A wellbeing, fitness or productivity app shows this week's habits at a glance and lets people mark any day so far with one tap, with streaks and a weekly target.
mobile-habit-grid.avoidWhen: You need long-range history (months or a year heatmap), habits measured in amounts rather than done or not done, or a single habit's detail view.
integration: Pass `habits` ({ id, name, icon, target, streak, paused }), the seven `days` and `todayIndex`; days after today are disabled.

Keep marks in your store with `value` and `onValueChange(next, change)`, and persist through `onToggle(change, signal)`: the cell fills at once, and a rejection rolls it back with a shake and a retry note.
`streak` is the run before today; the component adds today's mark, so send the server's figure rather than recomputing it on the client.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify touch, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-focus-session.useWhen: A single focus or pomodoro session on a phone: set the length on a dial, watch the time run down, pause or finish, and log the minutes against a daily goal.
mobile-focus-session.avoidWhen: Scheduling a day of tasks, tracking habits over weeks, or a background timer that must keep running and notify while the app is closed.
integration: The component runs its own clock from wall time, so it survives dropped frames. Use initialPhase and defaultElapsedSeconds to resume a session in progress, and phase to drive it from outside (a change plays like a tap).

onPhaseChange reports ready, running, paused and finished; onComplete receives { intention, plannedMinutes, focusedMinutes, completed } once per session. Persist it and pass the day's sessions back as completedToday.

presets, defaultMinutes and maxMinutes (one turn of the dial) set the lengths; dailyGoalMinutes sets the goal track. defaultDoNotDisturb and onDoNotDisturbChange wire the moon button to your own focus mode.

accent recolours the arc, its head and the live segment. Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once); background timing and notifications belong to the host.

mobile-day-planner.useWhen: A calendar, planner or focus app shows one day as a timeline and lets people move an event by dragging it, with clashes flagged and an explicit confirm before the calendar changes.
mobile-day-planner.avoidWhen: You need a week or month grid, multi-day or all-day events, creating events by dragging on empty time, or several people's calendars side by side.
integration: Pass `events` with `startMinute` and `endMinute` in local minutes after midnight; set `editable: false` with an `unavailableReason` for events the person doesn't own.

`onReschedule({ event, startMinute, endMinute, conflicts }, signal)` runs when Move is pressed; resolve once your calendar accepts it, reject to keep the proposal on screen with a retry. Send the updated `events` afterwards.
Set `dayStart`, `dayEnd` and `minuteStep` to your product's working day and grid; leave `nowMinute` out on days other than today. `allowOverlap` decides whether a clash can be confirmed.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify the drag, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-journal-prompt.useWhen: A journaling, therapy-adjacent or wellbeing app offers a few reflection prompts and a calm place to answer them, with drafts that survive switching prompts and an explicit keep.
mobile-journal-prompt.avoidWhen: You need long-form documents with formatting, a feed of past entries, or free writing with no prompts; a plain editor or list fits better.
integration: Pass `prompts` ({ id, title, question, guidance }) and the answers already kept as `answers` ({ promptId, text, updatedLabel }); kept prompts show a chip on their card.

`onSave({ prompt, text, previous }, signal)` runs when the person keeps an answer. Resolve once it's stored; reject to show the error with the words untouched. Pass `timeLabel` so the stamp matches your clock.
Control the current prompt with `selectedId` and `onSelectionChange` if your app deep-links to one; `streak` and `wordGoal` come from your own data and never block keeping.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify the keyboard, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-reading-progress.useWhen: An e-reader or audiobook library screen showing how far someone is through a book, its chapters and saved pages, with one tap back into reading.
mobile-reading-progress.avoidWhen: Rendering the book itself, or tracking reading goals and streaks across many books.
integration: Supply the book (id, title, author, pages, cover colours), chapters with first pages, and currentPage. Bookmarks can be controlled (bookmarks + onBookmarksChange) or local (defaultBookmarks).
onResume({ bookId, chapterId, page }, signal) opens your reader at the chosen page: the reader's place, or wherever the page edge, a chapter or a bookmark pointed. Jumping never marks pages as read.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once. Verify the page-edge drag, larger text and assistive technology on target devices.

mobile-trip-itinerary.useWhen: A trip with several legs across time zones, where travellers need local times, delays and cancellations at a glance and a quick way into each booking.
mobile-trip-itinerary.avoidWhen: Searching or booking travel, live vehicle tracking, or a single flight's status card.
integration: Supply legs in travel order with ISO instants (with an offset or Z), an IANA timeZone, code, city and lat/lon per place, a status, optional revised times, the operator's note and booking details. Clocks and day headers are formatted in each place's own zone.

onOpenLeg(leg, signal) opens the boarding pass, ticket or ride in your app; Cancel aborts the signal and late answers to older requests are ignored. Pass now to decide the next leg; tightConnection flags short connections.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once. Verify scrolling, larger text and assistive technology on target devices.

mobile-packing-list.useWhen: A travel or kit checklist where weight matters, so people see a bag fill toward a limit as they pack and adjust quantities to stay under it.
mobile-packing-list.avoidWhen: A general to-do list with no notion of weight or capacity, or inventory that needs search, sorting and bulk editing.
integration: Pass `trip` as { destination, dates, bag, limitKg, tareKg } and `items` as { id, name, detail?, group, qty, grams, packed }. Sections follow the order groups first appear; the bag's own weight counts from the start.
`onChange(items, change)` fires on pack, unpack, quantity, remove and restore with the whole list. It can return a promise; reject or throw and the list rolls back with your message in the toast.
Over the limit the bag and weight turn red regardless of `accent`. Remove offers Undo, which restores the item to its place.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg. Check the checkbox targets, the stepper with VoiceOver and larger text on devices.

mobile-budget-envelope.useWhen: Letting someone move money between budget categories on a phone, with the month's unassigned balance updating as they drag and nothing saved until the host accepts.
mobile-budget-envelope.avoidWhen: Moving real money between accounts, showing transaction history or charts of past spending, or a budget that isn't zero-based.
integration: envelopes: { id, name, icon, budgeted, spent, lastPeriod? } with icons home, basket, fork, car, bolt, coins, ticket or gift. Pass a new array to replace what the screen has accepted; income minus the budgets is Ready to Assign.

onBudgetChange(change) receives { envelopeId, name, from, to, readyToAssign }. Resolve to accept (the row and hero count to the new value); reject or throw and the sheet keeps the draft, shakes once and offers a retry.
step sets the ruler's notch; typed amounts keep their cents. allowOverAssign lets a budget exceed what's ready to assign; otherwise the ruler rubber-bands at the limit and says why.

openId and onOpenChange drive the envelope sheet from outside (null or an unknown id closes it). accent recolours the open segment, the needle and a balanced month; red is reserved for overspent and over-assigned.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once). Check real devices for keyboard, large text and assistive technology.

mobile-voice-memo.useWhen: Playing back a recorded memo, interview or voice note where people scrub by dragging the waveform, jump between markers and read along with a timed transcript.
mobile-voice-memo.avoidWhen: Recording audio, editing or trimming a clip, or a music player with queues and artwork; use a now-playing screen for music.
integration: Supply measured peaks (0–1, evenly spaced, about six a second), markers and transcript sentences with start and end seconds. Without a transcript the screen shows a written empty state.

The screen runs the playhead clock. Mirror it into your audio engine with onPlayingChange(playing, position), onSeek(position) and onRateChange(rate); onMarkerAdd reports markers dropped at the playhead.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once for expo-blur and expo-linear-gradient. Verify gestures, larger text and assistive technology on target devices.

mobile-project-switcher.useWhen: Apps where people work across several projects or workspaces and switch often, and the project's home should change around them without a page load.
mobile-project-switcher.avoidWhen: Apps with a single workspace, switching accounts or organisations with separate sign-ins, or very long lists that need a full search screen.
integration: Pass `projects` with stable ids, a glyph, the figures the home shows (open issues, cycle, seven days of activity, recent items) and `locked` with the reason for projects the person can't open.

Control `value` and resolve `onValueChange(id, project)` once your session has switched; reject with an Error to keep the current project and show the message on its row. Use `open` and `onOpenChange` to drive the sheet, and `onRequestAccess` for locked rows.

Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (`npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps). The mark's flight measures on-screen positions, so test inside your navigation container on devices.

mobile-file-preview.useWhen: Reading a shared document on a phone before acting on it: skimming pages, jumping to the one with comments, then downloading or opening it elsewhere.
mobile-file-preview.avoidWhen: Editing documents, browsing a folder of many files, or previewing images and video where a media viewer fits better.
integration: Pass `file` metadata and a `renderPage(index, width)` that draws each page with your PDF or document renderer; heights follow A-series proportions (width × 1.414). Mark commented pages with `marks`.
Drive `status` from your renderer: loading, ready, unsupported or error, with `statusMessage` for specifics and `onRetry` for the error panel.

Implement `onDownload(file, report)` and call `report(fraction)` as bytes arrive; reject with an Error to show its message. Wire `onOpen`, `onShare` and `onBack`. Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (`npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps).

mobile-attachment-tray.useWhen: Picking several files to send into a conversation on a phone, with real previews, a visible size limit, uploads that finish in place and a send that lands as one message.
mobile-attachment-tray.avoidWhen: Browsing a whole file system, previewing a single document full screen, or sending files outside a conversation.
integration: files are TrayFile { id, name, kind, bytes, status?, progress?, detail?, reason? }. Update status and progress from your uploader; only ready files can be picked. Failed files show their reason and call onRetry(file) when tapped.
maxFiles and maxBytes are enforced where the pick happens: a refused tile shakes and the hint explains. The meter shows the running total against the limit.
onSend({ files, note, totalBytes }) sends the selection. Resolve and the tiles leave, the tray folds and a message lands in the thread; reject and the files and note stay with an error.

renderThumbnail(file) draws a real preview (an Image) in place of the bundled drawings. messages and recipient set the conversation behind the tray; tray and onTrayChange drive it from outside; onAdd shows a Browse button for your picker.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once). Check the keyboard with the growing note field on real devices.

mobile-meeting-preflight.useWhen: The moment before joining a video call: checking your camera, microphone and speaker, choosing devices and joining once you're ready.
mobile-meeting-preflight.avoidWhen: The in-call screen itself, scheduling meetings, or apps without camera or microphone access.
integration: Pass your camera view as preview and subscribe the mic meter with micLevel(emit), returning an unsubscribe. Supply devices per group with availability, and readiness checks; a blocked check disables Join and says why.

onJoin({ roomId, muted, cameraOn, backgroundBlur, devices }, signal) joins the room; resolve when you're in. Cancel aborts the signal, and a rejection keeps every setting and offers Retry. Device, mute, camera and blur changes are reported through their callbacks.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once. Request camera and microphone permissions in your app before showing this screen, and verify on target devices.

mobile-channel-thread.useWhen: Reading and replying to one threaded conversation in a team channel on a phone, with quoting, reactions and honest sending, sent and failed states for your reply.
mobile-channel-thread.avoidWhen: A one-to-one chat with bubbles, a channel's full message list, or a transport layer that needs delivery receipts from other people.
integration: root and replies are ThreadMessage { id, author, time, text, quoteId?, reactions?, attachment? }. A reply with quoteId shows the quoted reply above its text.
onSend({ text, quoteId }) posts a reply. It appears at once as Sending; resolve to mark it Sent; reject and it stays as Not sent with a tap to retry, so the text is never lost.
status drives the thread: loading shows placeholder rows, error shows a banner over the cached replies with Retry (onRetry), unavailable makes the composer read-only with statusMessage in your words.
onReact(messageId, kind, mine) reports reaction toggles (check, eyes, heart); counts update immediately. accent recolours the send button, your reactions and the quote you are replying to.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once). Verify keyboard avoidance and safe areas in the host app.

mobile-task-move.useWhen: Changing an issue's status on a phone where the workflow has rules: work-in-progress limits, columns that need approval, and a move that should be easy to take back.
mobile-task-move.avoidWhen: Rearranging many cards across a full board, free-form kanban with no workflow rules, or desktop drag-and-drop between columns.
integration: Pass `task` and the ordered `statuses` for its workflow. Give each column a `kind` so the glyph shows progress, a `count`, an optional `limit` and a `blockedReason` for rules the server enforces.

Implement `onMove({ task, from, to, note })` against your tracker and throw an Error with a readable message to refuse; the note is kept. `onUndo` is offered for `undoSeconds` after a successful move.

Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (`npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps), and check the puck drag inside your own scroll views and with VoiceOver's adjustable actions.

mobile-review-annotations.useWhen: Reviewing a still image or design on a phone, where comments are pinned to exact points, reviewers resolve them one by one and can drop a new pin by tapping the artwork.
mobile-review-annotations.avoidWhen: Reviewing video or multi-page documents, or threaded discussions that need full reply chains on screen.
integration: Pass the image as `artwork` (any element that fills its box) with its `aspectRatio`, and `annotations` as { id, x, y, author, initials, text, time, replies?, resolved? }, where x and y are the pin tip from 0 to 1 across the artwork.

`onResolve(id, resolved)` is optimistic and rolls back if it rejects. `onAdd({ x, y, text })` can resolve with the saved annotation to replace the local one; reject and the draft stays with your error.
Tapping a pin zooms to it and swiping the cards moves the camera; `defaultSelectedId` picks the first comment shown.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg. Test pin tap targets, the carousel with VoiceOver and the composer with the keyboard open on devices.

mobile-notification-digest.useWhen: A scheduled summary of notifications grouped by app, where people clear the backlog by swiping each one to read or snooze it and expect a quick Undo.
mobile-notification-digest.avoidWhen: A live notification feed that must show each push as it arrives, or an inbox where messages are opened and replied to in place.
integration: Pass `groups` as { id, app, icon, items } with items { id, title, body, time, timeSensitive? }. Icons are drawn monochrome glyphs: tasks, chat, calendar, bank, transit and parcel.

Reads and snoozes are optimistic. `onRead` and `onSnooze` (with the chosen { id, label, until } option) can return a promise; reject or throw and the notification comes back with your message in the toast. `onRestore` fires on Undo.
`defaultExpanded` opens one pile on first view; `nextSummary` sets the caught-up message.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg. The cards are glass over a drawn wallpaper; keep something with luminance behind them if you change the background.

mobile-sync-conflict.useWhen: Resolving a record that two people or devices edited offline, field by field, where each person should see both versions and physically pick one before the merge is saved.
mobile-sync-conflict.avoidWhen: Automatic last-write-wins sync, text documents that need a character-level merge, or conflicts with more than two versions of a field.
integration: Pass the two sides as `mine` and `theirs` ({ name, initials, device, deviceName, editedAt }), the conflicting fields as { id, label, mine, theirs } and any agreed fields as `settled` for context. Changed words are highlighted from a word diff of the two values.
Each card can be dragged over the other or kept with its button. `onChoose` reports every choice with { fieldId, choice, value } so you can keep a draft; `defaultChoices` resumes one.
`onSave` receives every resolution once all fields are chosen. Resolve to show the synced state; reject or throw to keep the choices and show your error message with a retry.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare apps run `npx install-expo-modules`). Check drag, VoiceOver and large text on devices.

mobile-offline-outbox.useWhen: A mobile app that saves work without signal and needs one place to see what is waiting, send it on demand and fix the changes a server turns down.
mobile-offline-outbox.avoidWhen: Apps that are always online, background sync you never surface to people, or resolving rich merge conflicts field by field.
integration: Supply `items` from your local queue with stable ids, a kind, size and saved time. Pass `network` from your connectivity listener: Wi-Fi drains automatically, mobile data waits for Send now, offline waits.

Implement `onSend` to apply one change and throw an Error with a readable message when the server rejects it; the message is shown on the row and in the sheet, and the change stays queued. Edited notes arrive with their new `body`.

Remove discarded changes in `onDiscard`. Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (run `npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps) and verify on devices with real connectivity changes.
